B: I felt anxious on the platform. I wanted to get to dinner. I tried to send a message, but I do not know whether it arrived. When I got to dinner, A wouldn't talk to me.

claims.text: A reports feeling unimportant.

claims.rationale: B explicitly reports this. Without B's narrative the report is unavailable.
claims.text: B reports feeling anxious.

claims.rationale: Without B's account, nothing speaks to B's motive. B says "I wanted to get to dinner," which does not fit someone arriving late in order to punish A.
claims.text: B arrived late in order to punish A.

claims.rationale: Explicitly established by the stipulated shared facts.
claims.text: B arrived after the booked dinner time.

claims.rationale: Only A says B seemed annoyed, and that is A's impression. B's account does not mention annoyance, so what B actually felt remains open.
claims.text: B was annoyed upon arrival.

claims.rationale: This cause is explicitly stipulated in shared facts; causal claims are not always unknown.
claims.text: The train cancellation prevented B from taking the planned train.

shared: A and B are adult partners. Dinner was booked for 7 pm. B arrived at 7:30 pm. A train cancellation prevented B from taking the planned train.
